title: Om Is All This
meter: Prose (the Upanishad mantras have no meter)
meterNote: The mantras of the Mandukya Upanishad are prose, not verse, so there is no meter to scan. Their rhythm comes from the chant. Notice how this mantra uses pada and matra, the same two words the meter scanner is built on.
translation: Om: this syllable is all this. Here is its explanation: the past, the present and the future, all of it is Om alone. And whatever else lies beyond the three times, that too is Om.
translation_hi: ॐ: यह अक्षर ही यह सब कुछ है। उसकी व्याख्या यह है: भूत, वर्तमान और भविष्य, यह सब ओंकार ही है। और जो कुछ तीनों कालों से परे है, वह भी ओंकार ही है।

words.note: iti marks the word as a quotation.
a + kshara (perishing): a syllable is 'what does not decay'.
Future participle: 'what will be'. Hindi भविष्य.

grammar: One root, three times: √भू gives भूत (past), भवत् (present) and भविष्यत् (future). Hindi still uses भूतकाल and भविष्यकाल.
Akshara: 'syllable' and 'imperishable' at once. The Upanishad means both.
Guna sandhi: तस्य + उप → तस्योप, like तस्योपरि in the peacock verse.
